sentences.text: Present 'Reference' under section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act was forwarded by the LAC, West District to adjudicate upon the competing claims of 2 Interested Persons (IP's) over the right to claim a share in the compensation awarded on account of compulsory acquisition of land under the LA Act, in village Mundka.
The land was acquired for the purpose of construction of Rohini Residential Scheme.
Total area of the land acquired was measuring 1703 bigha, 18 biswa.

The acquired area is covered by Award No. 03/DC(W)/2005-2006 dated 27.01.2006.
2.
Both the IP's were related to each other (both have since expired).
IP No 1 Nihalo Devi was the widow of Net Ram who had 1/4th share in the acquired land.
She got the acquired land mutated in her name (i.e. to the extent of 1/4th share of Net Ram) in the yr. 2000 by holding out that she was the only surviving legal heir of Net Ram.
IP No. 2 Sureshwati @ Suresh was the widowed daughter-in-law of late Net Ram i.e. wife of Net Ram's son Chander Bhan.
LAC No. 166/16 UOI Vs Nihalo Devi & Ors. 2/11 3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: IP No. 2 had expired in 2014, prior to the present Reference having been forwarded by the LAC but before her death, she had already sent her objection to the LAC office informing it that Nihalo Devi had fraudulently got the mutation carried out in her name by concealing material facts about her children - 2 sons and a daughter, and was also seeking to pocket the entire compensation.

IP No.
1 subsequently expired in 2017, during the pendency of the present Reference.

4. It had been averred in the claim of IP No. 1 that she is the joint bhumidhar/co-owner to the extent of 1/4th share in Khasra No. 23//20, 21, 22, 24, 25//2, 46//5/2 and 47//1/1 total measuring 19 Bigha 9 Biswas of Village Mundka, Delhi.

It had further been claimed that other share holders had already received compensation but due to objection of one Smt. Sureshwati W/o late Sh. Chander Bhan, no compensation payment was tendered to IP No. 1.

It had been further averred tht Smt. Sureshwati/IP No. 2 was the wife of predeceased son of IP No. 1 having no children and was living with her parents since the death of her husband Sh. Chander Bhan i.e. pre-deceased son of IP No. 1.

It had been claimed that IP No. 1 had also informed in writing through an application dated 25.02.2015 to the concerned LAC that after the death of Smt.
Sureshwati, the objections raised by Sureshwati before the LAC had become infructuous but instead of tendering payment to the IP No. 1, the present reference u/s 30-31 of L.A Act was forwarded to this Court.

It was thus asserted that LAC No. 166/16 UOI Vs Nihalo Devi & Ors. 3/11 the alleged objections, if any, are void and not sustainable as IP No. 1 is the recorded owner qua 1/4th share of the land comprised in the above noted Khasra numbers and hence, is exclusively entitled to receive the compensation assessed by the LAC for the aforesaid land.

and consequently, moved an application before this Court for being impleaded as legal heir of IP No. 2.
The application was strongly contested by IP No. 1 on the ground that applicant Pratibha Saini was never adopted by late Chander Bhan and late Sureshwati.

The said order was stated to have been challenged before D.C (West) under section 65 of the Delhi Land Revenue Act.
It has been claimed that Sh. Chander Bhan Saini and his wife had legally adopted Smt. Pratibha Saini.
Sh. Chander Bhan Saini unfortunately also expired on 29.11.1995.

Subsequently, the wife of Sh. Chander Bhan Saini had filed objections before the LAC, West LAC No. 166/16 UOI Vs Nihalo Devi & Ors. 7/11 against the awarded amount of compensation which is subject matter of the present reference.

Hon'ble High Court was of the view that a definitive finding on the aspect of adoption of the applicant by Chander Bhan and Sureshwati had not been given in the order dt.
9.3.2018.
Hence, the Hon'ble High Court directed this Court to decide the controversy afresh, in the backdrop of the evidence already led and section 11 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956.
At that stage, applicant led additional evidence in support of her legal heir application by examining her biological parents.

The matter LAC No. 166/16 UOI Vs Nihalo Devi & Ors. 8/11 was thereafter argued again on the limited issue of whether Ms. Pratibha Saini is the adoptive daughter of Chander Bhan and Sureshwati and hence, an legal heir of IP No. 2?

sentences.text: While deciding the application of Ms Pratibha Saini due regard was given to the additional evidence which was led by examining biological parents of Ms Pratibha Saini, as also extensive documentary evidence led on either behalf which was examined threadbare since the application of Ms Pratibha Saini to be impleaded as legal heir of IP No. 2 factually become a contest between Ms Pratibha Saini and legal heir of IP No. 1 Smt. Nihalo Devi to claim share in the compensation amount.

After having considered to the requirements of a valid adoption as laid down in Section 11 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956, evidence led by both the sides and the attending circumstances in the backdrop of documentary evidence led, this Court came to a definite LAC No. 166/16 UOI Vs Nihalo Devi & Ors. 9/11 conclusion that Ms Pratibha Saini was not the legally adopted daughter of IP No. 2 and her husband late Chander Bhan.

15.

Since the status of Smt. Premwati @ Prem Lata as legal heir of IP No. 1 being her daughter was not being disputed even by Ms Pratibha Saini, in the absence of any other claimant, the reference is answered in favour of Smt. Premwati @ Prem Lata.

Since the Will has not been proved in accordance with the law and has merely been exhibited, this Court is not relying upon the Will to allow the present claim.

However, as already highlighted above since status of Premwati @ Prem Lata of being the sole daughter of IP No. 1 was never in dispute,
the issue of right to claim compensation is decided in favour of legal heir of I.P. No. 1 Smt. Premwati @ Prem Lata.
